rule.listed_vector: 1 if any category term appears in SIDER 4.1 side effects for the drug or in the selected label's adverse-reactions, warnings, precautions or boxed-warning text, at any or no frequency; 0 if the drug has a source and no mention; null if neither source exists
rule.negative: no category term reaches 5% and EITHER the drug's own adult adverse-reaction table was parsed (it lists every reaction at or above its inclusion threshold, 2% or 5% in these labels, so a term absent from it is below that) OR, with SIDER frequencies only, every category concept that SIDER or the label names has a printed frequency below 5%
rule.not_applied: the 'twice placebo' half of the Highlights convention: SIDER placebo rows are not paired to drug rows by trial, so it cannot be applied uniformly
rule.null: otherwise: no frequency-bearing source, or a category concept is named (SIDER side effect, label prose) with no frequency anywhere. Unknown is never defaulted to negative: old labels name haloperidol's EPS and amitriptyline's dry mouth without a number. Synonyms ('weight gain' / 'weight increased') are one concept
rule.positive: a category term has a drug-arm incidence >= 5% in the drug's own adult adverse-reaction table (selected openFDA label), or a SIDER 4.1 non-placebo frequency row whose LOWER bound is >= 0.05
rule.postmarketing: SIDER rows described 'postmarketing' (stored as 0-0.001) are not frequency evidence: a spontaneous report has no denominator. They count toward the listed vector only
rule.why_5_percent: the incidence most US labels use for their Highlights 'most common adverse reactions'; the CIOMS 'common' boundary (1%) admits almost every term in a psychiatric label table. Fixed before any prevalence was computed; every per-term maximum is stored so another threshold can be applied without refetching
rule.why_lower_bound: SIDER encodes a frequency word as a range ('frequent' = 0.01-1); only the lower bound is a frequency the label actually asserts
